title: Yet public prayers addressed to the images themselves seem to clash with Nicaea II and Trent’s ban on seeking anything from an image
source_text: XX. Sed in quibusdam videtur Ecclesiae Romanae praxis non satis cum decretis Conciliorum ipsius concordare. Nam, ut supra vidimus, Synodus Nicena secunda, cum Anastasio, docet, Imagini non licere proskunein. Et similiter Synodus Tridentina ab imagine nihil esse petendum. Et tamen in publico Ecclesiae Romanae usu sunt quaedam precationes quae ad imagines ipsas diriguntur.
pass_a_gloss: But in some things the practice of the Roman Church seems not sufficiently to agree with the decrees of her own Councils. For, as we saw above, the second Nicene Synod, with Anastasius, teaches that it is not lawful to proskunein an image. And likewise the Tridentine Synod [teaches] that nothing is to be sought from an image. And yet in the public use of the Roman Church there are certain prayers which are directed to the images themselves.
pass_b_english: Practice strains the Councils: Nicaea II and Trent bar seeking from an image, yet Rome’s public use aims prayers at the images themselves.
